recommendations.title: The Book of the New Sun

recommendations.title: Domination and the Arts of Resistance

recommendations.title: The Raw Shark Texts

recommendations.reason: Their want list reveals a love for formally inventive, genre-blending fiction (House of Leaves already read; The Magus, Piranesi, Cloud Atlas on want list), and this conceptual thriller about a man hunted by a 'conceptual shark' sits squarely at that intersection.

recommendations.title: The Sparsholt Affair
recommendations.author: Alan Hollinghurst
recommendations.reason: Their interest in sweeping literary fiction across time (The House of the Spirits, Fingersmith, The Books of Jacob on want list) combined with LGBTQ+ titles like Carol and A Marvellous Light suggests they would love this elegant multigenerational novel of desire and secrets.

recommendations.title: Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy
recommendations.author: John le Carré
recommendations.reason: Having already read The Spy Who Came In from the Cold and with Our Kind of Traitor on their want list, this masterful espionage novel featuring George Smiley is the essential next le Carré they are missing.

recommendations.title: The Unconsoled
recommendations.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
recommendations.reason: Having read Never Let Me Go and with The Pale King and The Unbearable Lightness of Being on their want list, this disorienting, dreamlike novel about memory and obligation matches their taste for literary fiction that pushes formal boundaries.

recommendations.title: A Tomb for Boris Davidovich
recommendations.author: Danilo Kiš
recommendations.reason: Their appetite for dark, formally ambitious literary fiction engaging history and moral reckoning (Blood Meridian already read; Absalom Absalom!, The Books of Jacob on want list) makes this devastating cycle of stories about Stalinist persecution a natural and essential fit.

recommendations.title: The Passage of Power
recommendations.author: Robert A. Caro
recommendations.reason: Their interest in political history through books like 'A Promised Land,' 'All the King's Men,' and 'Imperium' suggests they'd be captivated by Caro's masterful blend of political intrigue, power, and American history.

recommendations.title: The Terror of Living
recommendations.author: Urban Waite
recommendations.reason: Their affinity for taut, literary crime fiction like 'Blacktop Wasteland,' 'Razorblade Tears,' and 'Mystic River' points toward this dark, atmospheric Pacific Northwest thriller with beautifully spare prose.

recommendations.title: The Sunken Land Begins to Rise Again
recommendations.author: M. John Harrison
recommendations.reason: Their taste for literary strange fiction spanning Ballard's 'Concrete Island,' Fowles' 'The Magus,' and T. Kingfisher's work suggests they'd respond deeply to Harrison's unsettling, dreamlike contemporary Gothic.

recommendations.title: A Fire Upon the Deep
recommendations.author: Vernor Vinge
recommendations.reason: Their broad science fiction appetite spanning Lem's 'Solaris,' Simmons' 'Hyperion,' and Corey's 'Leviathan Wakes' makes this landmark, ideas-dense space opera a natural fit.

recommendations.title: The Unconsoled
recommendations.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
recommendations.reason: Their love of formally disorienting literary fiction like 'House of Leaves' and 'The Magus,' combined with their admiration for Ishiguro's 'Never Let Me Go' and 'Klara and the Sun,' makes this dreamlike, unsettling novel a compelling next step.

recommendations.title: Falling Man
recommendations.author: Don DeLillo
recommendations.reason: Their interest in literary fiction engaging with politics, culture, and crisis — seen through 'The Circle,' 'Screen People,' and 'The Deluge' — aligns with DeLillo's unflinching post-9/11 psychological reckoning.

recommendations.title: The Raw Shark Texts
recommendations.author: Steven Hall
recommendations.reason: Their appetite for formally inventive, reality-bending fiction like 'House of Leaves,' 'Cloud Atlas,' and 'How to Live Safely in a Science Fictional Universe' makes this genre-defying conceptual thriller an ideal match.

recommendations.title: The Helliconia Trilogy
recommendations.author: Brian W. Aldiss
recommendations.reason: Their want-to-read listing of Aldiss's 'Hothouse' alongside ecological dystopias like 'The Deluge' and 'Blue Skies' suggests they'd be enthralled by his sweeping, climate-obsessed planetary epic.

recommendations.title: The Terror of Living
recommendations.author: Urban Waite
recommendations.reason: The bleak, rural noir atmosphere and morally complex characters echo the crime fiction of S.A. Cosby and Dennis Lehane that dominates their thriller interests.

recommendations.author: Steven Hall
recommendations.reason: The genre-blending metafictional horror and labyrinthine mystery closely mirrors the appeal of House of Leaves, Night Film, and the experimental literary fiction throughout their list.

recommendations.title: The Children of Men
recommendations.author: P.D. James
recommendations.reason: Their deep investment in dystopian fiction from Parable of the Sower to The Light Pirate makes this existential near-future thriller a clear match for their taste.

recommendations.title: The Helliconia Trilogy
recommendations.author: Brian W. Aldiss
recommendations.reason: Their interest in Aldiss's Hothouse signals an appetite for ambitious, ecological science fiction world-building on a grand scale.

recommendations.title: The Secret House of Death
recommendations.author: Ruth Rendell
recommendations.reason: The psychological suspense, unreliable domestic settings, and slow-burn dread found across their thriller picks from Paula Hawkins to Ian McEwan align perfectly with Rendell's style.

recommendations.title: Butcher's Crossing
recommendations.author: John Williams
recommendations.reason: Having Augustus by John Williams on their list and showing strong interest in historical adventure like Undaunted Courage, this brutal and literary Western would be a compelling next read from the same author.

recommendations.title: The End of the Affair
recommendations.author: Graham Greene
recommendations.reason: Their taste for morally serious literary fiction with psychological depth, seen in picks from Ian McEwan, Milan Kundera, and Bret Easton Ellis, aligns closely with Greene's brooding, introspective style.

recommendations.title: The Unconsoled
recommendations.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
recommendations.reason: With multiple Ishiguro books already read and enjoyed, this surreal, dreamlike novel about memory and identity bridges their clear interests in literary fiction, psychological complexity, and the uncanny.

recommendations.title: The Secret House
recommendations.author: David Bodanis
recommendations.reason: Their interest in popular science titles by Greene, Dawkins, and Gleick suggests they'd enjoy this microscopic exploration of hidden scientific phenomena in everyday life.

recommendations.reason: Their love of historical crime fiction spanning Eye of the Needle, Fingersmith, and Small Mercies points toward this dark, psychologically rich Victorian-era detective novel.

recommendations.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
recommendations.reason: Their extensive interest in literary science fiction exploring dystopia, society, and philosophy (Parable of the Sower, The Left Hand of Darkness implied by Butler interest, Solaris, Cloud Atlas) makes this politically rich, dual-world novel an essential fit.

recommendations.title: The Terror of Living
recommendations.author: Urban Waite
recommendations.reason: Their taste for tense, literary crime fiction with morally complex characters in unforgiving landscapes (Blacktop Wasteland, Razorblade Tears already read, No Country for Old Men implied by McCarthy interest) makes this spare, brutal debut thriller a strong match.

recommendations.title: Pirate Cinema
recommendations.author: Cory Doctorow
recommendations.reason: Their interest in dystopian fiction examining surveillance, media, and corporate power (The Circle, V for Vendetta, Chain-Gang All-Stars, Screen People on their list) aligns well with this near-future novel about youth revolt against draconian internet censorship.

recommendations.title: My Year of Rest and Relaxation
recommendations.author: Ottessa Moshfegh
recommendations.reason: Their interest in dark, psychologically intense literary fiction featuring morally uncomfortable protagonists (Lolita, The Rules of Attraction, Beautiful World Where Are You, The Guest) suggests they would be drawn to this bleak, sardonic portrait of dissociation and self-destruction.

recommendations.title: The Grip of It
recommendations.author: Jac Jemc
recommendations.reason: Their strong appetite for literary haunted-house horror that blurs psychological and supernatural dread (The Haunting of Hill House already read, The Last House on Needless Street, Hidden Pictures, The September House) makes this formally inventive, deeply unsettling debut an ideal recommendation.

recommendations.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes
recommendations.author: Ray Bradbury
recommendations.reason: Their love of atmospheric, literary horror and dark fantasy with a mythic quality (The Night Circus, It, We Have Always Lived in the Castle) makes this lyrical, deeply unsettling tale of a sinister carnival arriving in a small town a natural fit.

recommendations.title: The Little Stranger
recommendations.author: Sarah Waters
recommendations.reason: Their appreciation for psychologically ambiguous, slow-burn gothic horror with literary weight (Fingersmith already on their list, The Haunting of Hill House, Dark Matter, The Comfort of Strangers) makes Waters's deeply unsettling postwar haunted-house novel an ideal next read.
